digest.key_takeaway:
A quick roundup of AI and developer news since the last digest.


  
  
  AI models & research




Cognition releases SWE-2.1, with a 600 tokens/s Ultrafast mode: Cognition's new in-house coding model is RL-trained on Moonshot's open-weight Kimi K3 and roughly doubles SWE-2's Terminal-Bench 4.1 score, though by Cognition's own numbers it still trails Claude Opus 5.5 on every benchmark. An Ultrafast version runs the same model on Cerebras hardware at about 10x the speed, and a SWE-2.1 Cyber variant with looser safeguards now powers Devin Security scans. The New Stack

articles.title: Netflix Builds Quasar to Measure the Blast Radius of Library API Changes
articles.summary: Netflix developed Quasar, an internal tool that combines semantic code indexing and API comparisons to identify downstream consumers affected by library changes. Using SCIP, Amazon S3, and Athena, it traces API references across repositories, helping maintainers assess migration impact and make informed release decisions. Netflix is also exploring agent-assisted consumer migrations. By Leela Kumili

articles.title: We turned τ-bench around to grade the agent's instructions, not the agent
articles.summary:
Agent benchmarks ask how well an agent follows its instructions. We wanted to ask one step up: how good are the instructions in the first place?

Agents are getting good at doing what they're told. Give a current model a clear policy and the right tools and it mostly sticks to it, which is exactly what benchmarks like τ-bench measure. So the weak link is moving upstream. Someone has to write that policy, and the person who knows the business is rarely the person who knows how to write rules a machine can act on. articles.title: RAG is Dead. MIT Just Built Something Better.
articles.summary:
I thought RAG was the answer

For 2 years, I built AI apps with RAG. Vector DB. Chunking. Embeddings. The whole thing.

It worked. Kind of.

But the problems kept coming:



Retrieval noise — wrong chunks, wrong context

Lost connections — cross-document relationships? Gone

Catastrophic forgetting — new docs overwrite old knowledge

Slow as hell — similarity search at scale is expensive


I kept adding layers. Better chunking. Re-ranking. Hybrid search.

But it felt like putting band-aids on a broken system.

articles.title: Shift subtitle timestamps without silently clipping the first cue
articles.summary:
A fixed subtitle delay is easy to correct until a negative offset moves a cue before the start of the video. Clamping only its start to zero shortens that cue; clamping both boundaries can create a zero-duration cue. A small validation function makes the choice explicit.

Disclosure: I develop TokTranscript. This tutorial was generated by an AI agent; the included examples were executed locally. It is a standalone programming example, not a claim about the service's internal implementation.

articles.title: Vercel Sandbox alternatives: when to look past it and where to go
articles.summary:
Vercel Sandbox is a strong default if your app already deploys on Vercel. Each sandbox is a Firecracker microVM, the meter charges CPU only while code is using it, sandboxes persist by default, and there are 19 regions. The reasons to look elsewhere are rarely about the boundary. They are about account shape, box size, what happens around the agent, and where the hardware lives.

We build Sandscale, one of the options below. Vercel facts are from the Vercel Sandbox docs and pricing and quotas as of November 2026; other vendors' facts are from their own pages, linked at the end.

articles.title: Presentation: From Fan-Out to Fast: Sub-100ms API Design in Distributed Systems
articles.summary: Saranya Vedagiri explains how to design resilient, low-latency distributed APIs under 100ms. Drawing on practical scale at eBay, she discusses hop-by-hop latency budgets, async fanout tradeoffs, thread pool sizing, caching, and circuit breakers. Learn actionable strategies to eliminate tail-latency bottlenecks and establish performance-first engineering practices. By Saranya Vedagiri

articles.title: Speculative Decoding Makes Tool Calls Faster. Agents Need a Cache.
articles.summary:
Benchmarks with Qwen3 and Llama on llama.cpp show a draft model sped up code, JSON, and tool calls up to 1.7x, while uncached agent loops ran 6% slower.
The post Speculative Decoding Makes Tool Calls Faster. Agents Need a Cache. appeared first on Towards Data Science.

articles.title: Code Mode vs. Tool Calling Benchmarks Find a 16-Tool Crossover
articles.summary:
For agent builders with many MCP integrations, Code Mode was 120x cheaper and 18x faster on 100-item fan-outs but less reliable on single lookups.
The post Code Mode vs. Tool Calling Benchmarks Find a 16-Tool Crossover appeared first on Towards Data Science.

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto VI proves why efficiency isn’t a virtue
articles.summary: On the same day that Anthropic entered the public market, a painstakingly human video game became one of most successful entertainment launches of all time.

articles.title: .NET MAUI 11 Makes CoreCLR the Default Runtime and Adds Incremental XAML Hot Reload
articles.summary: Microsoft released .NET 11 with a .NET MAUI update focused on product quality. CoreCLR is now the default runtime on all platforms, and XAML gets incremental hot reload, implicit namespaces and faster resource dictionaries. The release also adds device test templates and passkey support, and raises the minimum Android and Apple platform versions. By Edin Kapić

articles.title: ChatGPT Boosted Consultants' Scores, Not Their Knowledge
articles.summary:
Consultants gained 49 points on coding with AI, while apprentices also gained comprehension — which is why assisted work and expertise need separate names.
The post ChatGPT Boosted Consultants' Scores, Not Their Knowledge appeared first on Towards Data Science.

articles.title: Mock Service Worker Releases v3.0 with ESM-Only Build, Socket-Based Interception and GraphQL Subs
articles.summary: Mock Service Worker 3.0 is now ESM-only, requires Node.js 22 or later, and cuts package size from 416KB to 234KB. It adds GraphQL subscription support, protocol-specific entrypoints, and an experimental defineNetwork API. Node.js interception now works at the TCP and TLS level. Some users report test failures from newly intercepted OPTIONS preflight requests. By Daniel Curtis

articles.title: Shuffle the Questions to Catch an LLM That Memorized Its Benchmark
articles.summary:
Two short Python functions and a free Colab GPU score a model in about half an hour; a z above 3 merits a look, while a near-zero score is more of a shrug.
The post Shuffle the Questions to Catch an LLM That Memorized Its Benchmark appeared first on Towards Data Science.
